fork.description: Attacking two pieces at once with one piece
fork.warning: Watch out for knight forks especially - they can attack two valuable pieces simultaneously
fork.defense: Keep your valuable pieces (queen, rooks) on different colored squares from each other

pin.description: A piece cannot move because it would expose a more valuable piece behind it
pin.warning: Bishops and rooks love to create pins - watch the diagonals and files to your king
pin.defense: Break pins by moving the piece behind, blocking, or attacking the pinning piece

skewer.description: Forcing a valuable piece to move, exposing a piece behind it to capture
skewer.warning: Keep your king and queen off the same diagonal or file
skewer.defense: Interpose a less valuable piece or move to break the alignment

discovered_attack.description: Moving one piece reveals an attack from a piece behind it
discovered_attack.warning: Be careful when your opponent's pieces are lined up with a piece in front
discovered_attack.defense: Don't let your valuable pieces align with opponent's hidden attackers

double_attack.description: Creating two threats at once that can't both be defended
double_attack.warning: Queens are especially dangerous for double attacks
double_attack.defense: When you see one threat, always look for a second

back_rank.description: Checkmate threat on the back rank when the king has no escape
back_rank.warning: If your king is trapped behind pawns, a rook or queen can deliver mate
back_rank.defense: Create a 'luft' (escape square) by pushing h3/h6 or g3/g6

trapped_piece.description: A piece has no safe squares to move to
trapped_piece.warning: Knights on the edge and bishops without retreating squares are vulnerable
trapped_piece.defense: Always ensure your pieces have escape routes

pawn_storm.description: Advancing pawns toward your king to open lines for attack
pawn_storm.warning: When you castle opposite sides, expect a pawn storm
pawn_storm.defense: Counter-attack in the center or on your own wing

piece_invasion.description: Opponent's pieces penetrating into your territory
piece_invasion.warning: Rooks on the 7th rank and knights in your camp are very dangerous
piece_invasion.defense: Trade off invading pieces or create your own counterplay

weak_square.description: A square in your position that can no longer be defended by pawns
weak_square.warning: Opponent's pieces will try to occupy your weak squares
weak_square.defense: Use pieces to control weak squares if pawns can't

isolated_pawn.description: Targeting a pawn that has no neighboring pawns to defend it
isolated_pawn.warning: Isolated pawns become targets in the endgame
isolated_pawn.defense: Keep pieces active to compensate for the weakness

bishop_pair.description: Two bishops working together control many squares
bishop_pair.warning: In open positions, the bishop pair is very powerful
bishop_pair.defense: Keep the position closed or trade one of the bishops

space_advantage.description: Opponent controls more squares and has more room for pieces
space_advantage.warning: Cramped positions make it hard to coordinate pieces
space_advantage.defense: Look for pawn breaks to free your position

signs: rooks on g or h files
kingside_attack.counter: Counter in the center or on the queenside

signs: rooks on a or b files
queenside_attack.counter: Attack in the center or on the kingside

central_breakthrough.counter: Control the center with pieces or prepare your own break

piece_exchange_simplification.counter: Avoid trades if behind, seek activity
